tools.description: Search the icon catalog. Returns the closest matches whether or not any truly fits: read each result's title, description, tags and matched_fields before using it (see the server instructions). Without a query, lists the most popular / first assets.

query.description: Words to look for (prefix match over title, tags, category, description).

sort.description: Order of the returned set: relevance (default), az, za, popular.

sources.description: Restrict to these collections: bioart, bioicons, servier, scidraw, healthicons, reactome, openmoji, user. Default: all.

tags.description: Keep only assets with one of these tags (a whole tag, any case). Default: any.

tools.name: search_assets

tools.description: Everything the catalog knows about one asset: description, tags, license, credit line, image URL and size.
tools.name: get_asset

tools.description: The same drawing in its other colour schemes / styles (same source and title).
tools.name: asset_variants

tools.description: Look at an asset: returns its catalog thumbnail when max_side is at most 256 and one is available, otherwise its original PNG (up to 2 MB). The free hosted endpoint does not resize images.
tools.name: asset_image

tools.description: An asset's SVG markup, to adapt it ("like this icon but ..."): edit the markup rather than redrawing from scratch. Also says whether an adaptation may be submitted to the library under the asset's license. Servier and some uploads have no SVG; very detailed drawings are too large to edit as code (redraw from asset_image instead).

max_kb.description: Largest markup to return, in kilobytes (default 150, max 500).

tools.name: asset_svg

tools.description: Look at up to 12 catalog previews with asset IDs, titles, collections, licenses and credits. Uses published thumbnails where available. Use render_assets to show selected icons in the interactive gallery.

ids.description: Asset ids, in the order to show them (at most 12).

tools.name: preview_assets

tools.description: Show selected icons in an interactive gallery with previews, licenses, credit lines and PNG/SVG downloads. First call search_assets and judge which results fit, then pass up to 12 selected IDs. Returns usable text and links in clients without app UI.

ids.description: Selected asset IDs, in display order.

tools.name: render_assets

tools.description: Page through a collection, optionally one category (see list_categories).
tools.name: browse_assets

tools.description: The collections in the catalog with their sizes and licenses.
tools.name: list_sources

tools.description: Run one read-only SQL statement (SQLite) against the catalog, e.g. to count, group or search with your own conditions. See db_schema first. Rows are capped.
tools.name: sql_query

tools.description: The catalog's tables and indexes, with notes on full-text search.
tools.name: db_schema

tools.description: Shared slide templates (whole slide layouts users published from the BioCartoon editor), newest first. Optional word filter.

query.description: Words that must appear in the title, description or category.

tools.name: list_templates

tools.description: The thumbnail of a shared template, to see its layout.
tools.name: template_image

tools.description: Submit one illustration to the shared BioCartoon library. Give the image as exactly one of svg, image, image_url or image_base64. It is held for review and published once a reviewer approves it; returns the submission id. Only call this after showing the user the image and these details and getting their go-ahead (rights_confirmed). The free hosted endpoint accepts PNG or SVG up to 2 MB. Convert or resize other image formats with the local biocartoon command before submitting.

category.description: Its category: a BioCartoon category slug (cells, cells.cell_types, lab_and_techniques.lab_equipment, ...) or free text.

credit.description: The name to credit (the user's name or handle, as they choose). Default: anonymous. CC-BY-4.0 needs one.

derived_from.description: The id of the library asset this is adapted from, if any (e.g. BA001505). Required for an adaptation: its license decides whether and how it may be submitted, and the original's credit line is added to the description.

email.description: Optional contact address for the reviewers (never published).

generative_ai_details.description: How generative AI was used, e.g. the model and what the user changed by hand (up to 500 characters).

generative_ai_used.description: Whether generative AI made any part of it. True for anything you drew or generated.

image.description: An image file from the conversation (ChatGPT passes generated or uploaded images this way).

image_base64.description: A PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, base64-encoded (a data: URL works too).

image_url.description: An https URL the image can be downloaded from.

license.description: CC0-1.0 (anyone may use it, no credit needed) or CC-BY-4.0 (credit required; only for artwork made without generative AI).

rights_confirmed.description: True only once the user has confirmed they may share this image under the license, and wants it submitted.

svg.description: The illustration as SVG markup (one complete <svg> element with a viewBox; no scripts, external links or web fonts).

tags.description: Words to find it by (up to 20, 40 characters each).

title.description: Name of the illustration, as people would search for it (up to 80 characters), e.g. "Pyramidal neuron".

tools.name: submit_artwork

tools.description: Where submissions are in review: pending, approved (it joins the catalog at the next publish) or rejected.
tools.name: submission_status
